items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
Picture words chosen from lib/src/alphabet/alphabet_data.dart; confirm each picture file clearly shows its word.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT words_pictures: the approved pilot template (3 picture words that each begin with their letter, all 3 pictures exist). Demonstrate has 6 steps (the puzzle is shown with both pictures it talks about). Letter options come from a widened pool of earlier letters. Check = hear-word-to-letter, find the word, name the picture (no caption); remediation = sound-first explanation plus the 'which word does NOT begin' puzzle and alternate items.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
Picture words chosen from lib/src/alphabet/alphabet_data.dart; confirm each picture file clearly shows its word.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT words_pictures: the approved pilot template (3 picture words that each begin with their letter, all 3 pictures exist). Demonstrate has 6 steps (the puzzle is shown with both pictures it talks about). Letter options come from a widened pool of earlier letters. Check = hear-word-to-letter, find the word, name the picture (no caption); remediation = sound-first explanation plus the 'which word does NOT begin' puzzle and alternate items.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (ऊन) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

One of the three source picture words is a number picture (counted objects); name-the-picture items are therefore not used in this lesson and the picture appears only in teaching steps with its caption.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
Picture words chosen from lib/src/alphabet/alphabet_data.dart; confirm each picture file clearly shows its word.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT words_pictures: the approved pilot template (3 picture words that each begin with their letter, all 3 pictures exist). Demonstrate has 6 steps (the puzzle is shown with both pictures it talks about). Letter options come from a widened pool of earlier letters. Check = hear-word-to-letter, find the word, name the picture (no caption); remediation = sound-first explanation plus the 'which word does NOT begin' puzzle and alternate items.

Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
Letter with anusvara/visarga: text-to-speech may not read it as the intended sound; native speaker to confirm.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
Rarely used or conjunct letter: educator to confirm it belongs in a Level 1 recognition set and what it is called.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (ஆடு) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (இலை) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source word 'ஈ' does not begin with exactly this letter (it begins with the letter plus a vowel sign, or is the letter itself), so no 'begins with' claim is made
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
Picture words chosen from lib/src/alphabet/alphabet_data.dart; confirm each picture file clearly shows its word.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT words_pictures: the approved pilot template (3 picture words that each begin with their letter, all 3 pictures exist). Demonstrate has 6 steps (the puzzle is shown with both pictures it talks about). Letter options come from a widened pool of earlier letters. Check = hear-word-to-letter, find the word, name the picture (no caption); remediation = sound-first explanation plus the 'which word does NOT begin' puzzle and alternate items.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
Picture words chosen from lib/src/alphabet/alphabet_data.dart; confirm each picture file clearly shows its word.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT words_pictures: the approved pilot template (3 picture words that each begin with their letter, all 3 pictures exist). Demonstrate has 6 steps (the puzzle is shown with both pictures it talks about). Letter options come from a widened pool of earlier letters. Check = hear-word-to-letter, find the word, name the picture (no caption); remediation = sound-first explanation plus the 'which word does NOT begin' puzzle and alternate items.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (எலி) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

One of the three source picture words is a number picture (counted objects); name-the-picture items are therefore not used in this lesson and the picture appears only in teaching steps with its caption.

The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (ஏணி) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

One of the three source picture words is a number picture (counted objects); name-the-picture items are therefore not used in this lesson and the picture appears only in teaching steps with its caption.

Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

One of the three source picture words is a number picture (counted objects); name-the-picture items are therefore not used in this lesson and the picture appears only in teaching steps with its caption.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (ஒட்டகம்) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

Only the target letter's picture word (ஓடை) is used (teaching steps and the heard-word items); the other two option letters have no usable picture word, so there are no pick-the-word or name-the-picture items.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_with_word: the letter has one picture word that begins with it, but the other two option letters have no usable word or no picture file, so the pick-the-word and name-the-picture tasks are NOT used. Word is used in teaching steps and in heard-word-to-letter items (audio, so a missing picture never leaks the answer). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose).

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source word 'ஔவை' is a person's name and has no picture
Rarely used or conjunct letter: educator to confirm it belongs in a Level 1 recognition set and what it is called.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.

No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source word 'கல்' does not begin with exactly this letter (it begins with the letter plus a vowel sign, or is the letter itself), so no 'begins with' claim is made
Tamil pure consonant (pulli) letter: the bare letter is likely misread by text-to-speech (it may say the consonant with an 'a' or spell it); native speaker to confirm how to speak it.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.

items_to_review: Every sentence (text, speech, prompts, hints, feedback, explanations) is AI-written and UNVERIFIED by a native speaker: grammar, naturalness, register, age suitability.
Text-to-speech in the lesson locale was not heard: how a bare letter is read (letter name versus sound, vowel length) and every sentence.

The letter wording ('which letter', 'sound of the letter', 'big letter' for the on-screen letter) and the negative item 'which letter is NOT ...' need native and educator confirmation for a 3-4 year old.
The letters used as wrong options are the next two letters of the sequence and (in some items) the previous letter, chosen by order not by visual similarity; confusable pairs were not designed.
No picture word is used for this letter. Reason: the source has no picture word for this letter
Tamil pure consonant (pulli) letter: the bare letter is likely misread by text-to-speech (it may say the consonant with an 'a' or spell it); native speaker to confirm how to speak it.
notes: ID, title, level, prerequisites and locale are copied from the existing recognition lesson in lib/src/curriculum.dart; the existing one-question lesson (letter spoken, three letters as options) is unchanged.

GUESS RATE: every check and remediation-check item has exactly 3 options and no hints (blind guess 33%; passing 2 of 3 by guessing alone about 26%). Guided and practice not-letter / not-word items have 2 options (as in the pilot); they are never used in a check because with three options two would be right.
Pass marks, cycle limit and the 'needs support' rule are data fields (mastery); after the limit the UI offers parent support and lets the child continue.
No tracing and no stroke order is taught anywhere.
Audio-only items (visual none) need a replay button and a visual fallback if text-to-speech fails (UI decision).

LIMITATION: the source gives each lesson only its own letter, two neighbouring letters and (sometimes) a picture word. Variety inside a lesson is therefore limited: items differ by task, wording, option set and answer position, but a child can still learn the small option sets by memory. More human-approved letters and picture words are needed to widen the check.

VARIANT letter_only: no usable picture word. Tasks: look-and-match (guided), listen-and-pick, and the 'which letter is NOT ...' puzzle (guided/practice only). Wrong letters come from the lesson's own two options plus letters taught earlier (nearest first); no (answer, option set) repeats in the lesson; practice item 6 and check item 3 are spaced reviews of the previous letter (field purpose). Check = hear-letter, hear-the-sound wording, previous-letter review.
